text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- The defense ministers of the Baltic and Nordic states are meeting in the Estonian island of Saaremaa to discuss regional security.
- Three people were killed and one was critically injured when a train smashed into a car.
- The government has applied for an additional 56 million kroons from the supplementary budget.
- Interior Minister Robert Lepiskon said that Estonia will have to take measures against illegal residents.
- Estonian Water Works has recommended that the town of Paide build a new water supply system. Water quality in the town has worsened in recent years.
- Finish and French consultants are preparing a traffic safety programme for Estonia.
- Estonian Prime Minister Mart Siimann told the paper that Estonia will not devalue the kroon.
- The Baltic Express passenger railway route between Tallinn and the Lithuanian-Polish border will be closed by September. The route, which was opened in 1993, lost 18 million kroons last year.
